sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Haralson County
sections.html:
Haralson County sits in northwest Georgia on the Alabama line, with the courthouse in Buchanan. The newest federal estimate puts population at 33,066, which is 10.5% above the April 2020 base.

Property tax splits across two desks. The assessors appraise each parcel and take exemption filings. The Tax Commissioner builds the digest, issues bills and collects. The commissioner has no say over value or millage. Those come from the assessors and from the county commissioners and the other taxing bodies such as cities and schools.

  • Board of Tax Assessors: 4266 GA Highway 120, Buchanan, 770-646-2022, weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Tax Commissioner: 770-646-2020 for payment and billing questions.
  • Towns inside the county: Bremen, Buchanan, Tallapoosa and Waco. Ask the clerk in the town where the house sits whether it sends its own bill.

Four incorporated places and three small unincorporated communities make up the county. Bremen is the largest city, at about 6,500 residents, followed by Tallapoosa at roughly 3,155, Buchanan at 1,159 and Waco at 522. Budapest, Draketown and Felton are unincorporated.

A city may levy its own tax and have its clerk bill it, unless the city and county agreed to one combined bill. A Bremen or Tallapoosa address can therefore mean two statements, while a house in an unincorporated community like Felton or Draketown sees only the county bill. Two public school systems operate here, so confirm which district a house falls in before you set a price.

December 1 is the payment deadline for land and houses. Mobile homes are billed for April 1. Interest waits until 60 days after the bill's postmark, then builds monthly at a rate pegged to prime.

Land and housesDecember 1Monthly interest plus 5% at each 120 day mark, capped at 20%

The bill is built from the assessors' value times 40 percent, which gives the assessed value. The millage rate from the commissioners and other levying bodies is then applied to that figure.

The Tax Commissioner's office also handles tag renewals, titles, mobile home decals, timber tax and handicap placards. The title desk stops processing at 4 p.m., so plan a closing-day errand with that in mind.

Appeals go in writing to the assessors before the cutoff printed on the yearly notice. Read the notice the day it arrives and mark the date, because late appeals are not taken.

The assessors define market value as the price an informed buyer and a willing seller would agree to in an arm's length deal. The notice also shows estimated taxes based on the prior year's millage, so the real bill can differ once the commissioners and the Board of Education set rates, usually between July and August.

Appeals volume has been heavy. When appeals pass the 3 percent threshold in O.C.G.A. 48-5-311, the board gets an extra 180 days to decide and notify owners. Anyone with an open appeal can call 770-646-2022 or email the assessors for status. Field appraisers may visit a property under O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1 and carry photo identification in a marked county vehicle.

The homestead exemption is the common one, and owners file with the Tax Commissioner's office. Ownership on New Year's Day plus an April 1 filing earns the current year's benefit. A late application waits until the next calendar year.

  • Homestead: applies to the house and its land when you live there as your legal residence. A person away for health reasons is not denied, and a family member or friend can notify the office for them.
  • Conservation use and preferential agricultural assessment: both use a 10 year covenant, and apply between January 2 and April 1. Preferential assessment generally gives a 25 percent advantage, and conservation use can save more than 50 percent in some cases.
  • Residential transitional assessment: a 10 year covenant for land moving from residential to commercial use.

Covenants matter in a sale. A farm or timber tract under a 10 year covenant carries obligations the buyer has to continue, so ask the Specialized Assessment department at the assessors' office what a transfer does to the covenant before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: What a Haralson County seller should do about the tax bill
sections.html:
Phone the Tax Commissioner at 770-646-2020 to learn the parcel's balance and whether this year's bill exists yet. Bills fall due December 1, so a closing earlier in the year often happens before the statement exists, and the contract has to say who covers that gap.

Interest and penalties stack up after the due date. A buyer's title search will pick up unpaid taxes, so a written payoff figure from the commissioner helps the closing attorney.

  • Confirm whether you filed for homestead by April 1 and whether it applies to the buyer's first year.
  • For a mobile home, remember the April 1 due date, which is separate from the December 1 bill on land.
  • If the land is under a conservation or preferential agricultural covenant, ask the assessors what a transfer does to it.

A cash sale does not wait on a lender's underwriting, but the tax payoff still comes out at closing. Bring the commissioner's written figure and your deed information to the closing attorney.

  1. Call the commissioner for the parcel balance and ask whether the current bill has been issued.
  2. Ask the assessors whether any covenant or specialized assessment is on the land.
  3. Collect the written payoff and give it to the closing attorney before the contract date.
  4. Tell the buyer which statements to expect, including any city bill, so nobody is surprised after closing.

Haralson County is mid-priced for rural west Georgia. For 2020 to 2024 the middle value of an owned home is $227,500, the middle household income is $72,127 and the middle rent is $923.

The county has 13,861 housing units and 11,747 households, and 71.6% of homes are owner-occupied. Owners with a mortgage typically pay $1,673 a month. Builders pulled 159 permits in 2025, so new supply is modest and resale houses compete mainly with each other.

faqs.q: When is Haralson County property tax due?
faqs.a: December 1 for land and houses, April 1 for mobile homes. Interest builds monthly at a prime-linked rate. A 5% penalty hits at each 120 day mark, and penalties stop at 20%.

faqs.q: Which number do I call about a Haralson County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Commissioner's office at 770-646-2020 for billing and payment. Questions about value or appeals belong with the assessors at 770-646-2022.

faqs.q: What is the Haralson County homestead exemption deadline?
faqs.a: April 1. You must own the home on January 1 and file by the return deadline. A later filing is held until the following calendar year.

faqs.q: Does Haralson County offer a break for farmland?
faqs.a: Yes. Both conservation use and preferential agricultural assessment ask for a ten year covenant, with applications taken January 2 through April 1. Preferential assessment generally gives a 25 percent advantage over fair market value.

faqs.q: Why is my Haralson County appeal taking so long?
faqs.a: When appeals pass 3 percent of parcels or digest value, O.C.G.A. 48-5-311 gives the assessors an extra 180 days to rule. Call 770-646-2022 or email the assessors for the status of your appeal.
